fact: Agence Ecofin reports that the regulator ARCEP, presenting its 2026 draft budget of 6.2 billion FCFA on 15 April 2026, listed finishing the set-up of the universal service fund among its priorities for the year; the fund's framework, under law 18.002 of 17 January 2018 and a decree of February 2019, provides for broadband internet access in mairies, alongside schools, health centres, libraries and post offices.

The universal service fund, whose scope includes broadband access in mairies, is supervised and managed by the Comité de développement des communications électroniques (CDCE), a body set by law, with ARCEP selecting the operators that receive its money, as Agence Ecofin reports.

The universal service fund is fed mainly by a levy on telecom operators of 2% of their previous year's turnover, and may also take gifts, loans and grants from the state, local authorities or development partners, as Agence Ecofin reports.

The CDCE, the body that manages the universal service fund, began its activities in July 2025, and on 15 April 2026 ARCEP said the fund's effective set-up was planned for 2026; the fund was not yet in operation and no mairie is reported connected through it.
